releases.title: AllAuth React SDK 1.0.0: portable React authentication and same-origin proxy
releases.summary: The earliest retained public archive contains cookie-based React authentication, account and organisation components, and an app-bound server proxy.
notes: Includes AllAuthProvider, SignIn, SignUp, password recovery, UserButton, UserProfile and OrganizationSwitcher backed by native cookie sessions.
Provides inline multi-factor continuation and account security controls without exposing session credentials to browser code.
Packages the optional Better Auth UI provider integration and a server-only same-origin Next.js proxy; the portable React components do not require Next.js.

provenance.details: Reconstructed from the earliest retained allowlisted SDK archive, 1.0.0. The original publication date was not retained.

releases.title: AllAuth React SDK 1.1.0: managed application branding and email-first sign-in
releases.summary: Adds centrally managed application branding and refines the portable authentication forms.
notes: Loads and validates public application branding, including names, logos, support email, colours and attribution, through the same-origin SDK configuration endpoint.
Adds branding overrides and shared authentication headers and footers to the portable sign-in, signup and password recovery forms.
Refines email-first password sign-in presentation and packages a Google icon while retaining the existing client and server proxy.

releases.title: AllAuth React SDK 1.4.1: Apple, Microsoft and canonical OAuth callbacks
releases.summary: Adds environment-advertised social providers and improves signed callback handling in the Next.js proxy.
notes: SignIn and SignUp render Apple and Microsoft buttons when the selected environment advertises configured native providers.
The Next.js proxy canonicalizes query parameters before signing mobile Google callbacks, preserving repeated values and opaque OAuth data.
Allows Apple's checked HTTPS form_post callback while retaining other POST origin checks and native state verification.
Adds a separate optional owned-photo lifecycle capability; the capability does not itself enable or configure a provider.

releases.title: AllAuth React SDK 1.4.3 is available
releases.summary: Organisation permission and slug checks no longer reload the active organisation. The organisation manager verifies fully granted permissions in one request, reducing delays and request-limit errors. Existing APIs, sign-in flows and organisation permissions remain compatible. Upgrade your pinned SDK package and rebuild your application when convenient.
notes: Read-only organisation permission and slug checks no longer invalidate active organisation hooks.
Organisation managers with all required permissions use one combined native permission check; delegated permissions retain individual verification.
Optional SDK-version reports support advisory dashboard update notices without requiring access to customer source code.

provenance.details: Verified request-budget regression tests, package parity and the immutable 1.4.3 archive support this announcement.

releases.title: AllAuth React SDK 1.4.4 is available
releases.summary: The Next.js application proxy now forwards Retry-After from AllAuth so applications can honor a temporary session-check rate refusal. HTTP status, JSON error codes and cookie headers remain intact. Existing integrations receive the service-side session-check resilience fix without an SDK upgrade; update your pinned package and rebuild to forward the response header to browsers.
notes: The Next.js proxy forwards Retry-After unchanged for both JSON and streamed responses, including numeric delays and HTTP dates.
HTTP 429 status, the service's stable error code, separate Set-Cookie headers and existing request-signature behavior remain compatible.
No automatic retries, customer dependency upgrades, credential changes or completed session-result caching are introduced. Existing SDK versions continue to authenticate with the updated service.

provenance.details: Failing-first proxy regressions cover numeric and HTTP-date Retry-After values, JSON and streamed HTTP 429 replies, cookies and credential-header boundaries. Focused SDK and archived-client compatibility checks passed before publication.
